clue.text: Puzzle when bird is restricted by farmyard disease

indicators.note: the bird is hemmed in, so its letters sit inside the disease's letters

parts.note: BSE, bovine spongiform encephalopathy or mad cow disease
the emu is the usual crossword bird

explanation.surface: A farmer is baffled when a bird catches a disease that usually strikes cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemuse is to puzzle or bewilder someone, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Man perhaps in gym getting tender on the outside

indicators.note: the tender sits outside, wrapping round the gym letters

parts.note: a bid is a tender, an offer
PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: A man at the gym is sore all over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' looks like sore; it is an offer, BID.
explanation.definitionFit: Man is an example of a two-footed animal, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: German city with hospital demolished by one friend in local government office?

indicators.note: the hospital is knocked down, so its letter is removed

parts.note: Munich is in Bavaria, Germany
I is the Roman numeral for one
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A German city has torn down a hospital, with a friend in the council office.
explanation.definitionFit: Municipal describes the affairs of a town's local government, so it suits someone holding such office.

clue.text: Stay to get temperature taken — when one's this?

indicators.note: the temperature letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: to stick is to stay put

explanation.surface: A patient is told to stay in bed and have their temperature taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temperature taken' reads like a thermometer, but it means T is removed from STICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unwell is when a doctor would take one's temperature and tell one to stay in bed.

clue.text: Latin maybe is hard — time to go off and flop?

indicators.note: the time period departs from the word for Latin, leaving the rest

parts.note: Latin is an example of a language
an age is a long period of time
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A schoolchild finds Latin tough and wants time off to collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go off' takes AGE out of LANGUAGE, leaving LANGU.
explanation.definitionFit: To languish is to droop or lose vigour, which is what a plant does when it flops.

clue.text: Brief very quietly delving into issue

indicators.note: the quiet letters dig into the middle of the issue word

parts.note: to issue is to arise, emerge
PP, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quiet

explanation.surface: A short note is quietly investigating a matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' is a verb, not a short thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprise someone is to inform them, the same as to brief them.

clue.text: Accommodation with some beds nearby?

parts.note: the beds are flower beds rather than beds to sleep in, near a ground-floor home

explanation.surface: A guest house has some beds close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The beds that seem to be for sleeping are flower beds outside the window.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden flat is a ground-floor apartment opening onto a garden, flower beds included.

clue.text: I may represent this country

parts.note: in the NATO phonetic alphabet the letter I is spoken as a country's name

explanation.surface: Someone boasts they might represent their nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is not the speaker but the letter, which in radio spelling is named after a country.
explanation.definitionFit: India is the code word for the letter I in the NATO phonetic alphabet.

clue.text: Impulsive, as Harry and Helen are seen to be?

definitions.meaning: ... means rash, quick to act without thinking

definitions.text: as Harry and Helen are seen to be?
definitions.meaning: both names are headed by H, and H on a tap stands for hot

explanation.surface: Two people called Harry and Helen are thought to act on impulse.
explanation.walkthrough: Written down, each name begins with H, the letter on a hot tap, so they are headed by hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotheaded person acts rashly and without thought, which is impulsive.

clue.text: Half-hearted cry of derision when meeting snake and rodent

indicators.note: one of the two middle letters of the word, half its heart, is removed

parts.note: a jeer is a mocking cry
a boa is a large constricting snake

explanation.surface: A feeble jeer goes up when a snake meets a rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: The jerboa is a small desert rodent that hops on long hind legs.

clue.text: Confidence of a revolutionary faced with censure

indicators.note: the revolutionary has the censure in front of it, so the censure comes first

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: A revolutionary keeps his confidence despite being publicly condemned.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant self-assurance, a stylish kind of confidence.

clue.text: Gem that's very bad being put back in container

indicators.note: the reversed word is placed inside the container

parts.note: a pot is a container

indicators.note: put back means the word is turned around and read backwards

parts.note: dire means very bad

explanation.surface: A dreadful gem is returned to its box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being put back' reverses the word for very bad before it goes into the pot; 'that's' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green gemstone, a variety of olivine.

clue.text: Cubes of frozen stuff applied to wound ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word wound

parts.note: ice is frozen water

explanation.surface: Ice cubes are pressed against an injury to soothe it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dice are small cubes, and to dice food is to cut it into cubes.

clue.text: Get rid of scholar no longer showing benefits of education?

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school
being literate, able to read and write, is a benefit of schooling

explanation.surface: An educated person has lost all the learning they once showed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about a lapsed scholar, but 'scholar no longer' is a former pupil, an old boy, and the rest describes someone able to read and write.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe out or destroy completely, so it means to get rid of.

clue.text: Radioactive element that has "warm nuclei", roughly

indicators.note: roughly suggests the letters are only loosely in order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A radioactive element is said to have warm atomic nuclei.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawrencium is a synthetic radioactive element, atomic number 103.

clue.text: OAP wild with anger about hotel accommodation not suitable for his age group

definitions.text: accommodation not suitable for his age group

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the hotel letter
wild shows the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written: an old-age pensioner
taken as written
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An angry pensioner rages at being put up somewhere meant for a much younger crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' scrambles the two words into ORPANAGE, and 'about' wraps that round the hotel letter. An OAP is a British old-age pensioner.
explanation.definitionFit: An orphanage houses children, so a pensioner is far too old to be lodged there.

clue.text: Excessively admired sweetheart, not the first to get told off

indicators.note: the opening letter of the sweetheart word is dropped

parts.note: a lover is a sweetheart
to rate is an old word for to scold

explanation.surface: An adored sweetheart is scolded, and not for the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: Overrated means valued more highly than deserved, so admired to excess.

clue.text: Nameless chum under the influence of drugs?

indicators.note: the word chum loses N, the usual abbreviation for name

parts.note: a chum is a friend

explanation.surface: An unnamed pal appears to be high.
explanation.definitionFit: Fried is slang for intoxicated, or for having a frazzled mind from drink or drugs.

clue.text: Agreement to get tough, hiding depression

indicators.note: the toughening word conceals the depression inside it

parts.note: to inure is to harden or accustom to hardship
a dent is a small depression

explanation.surface: A tough negotiator conceals their low mood to reach a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: An indenture is a formal contract, especially binding an apprentice to a master.

clue.text: Mathematician showing hesitation about principle that's not right

indicators.note: the hesitation sound goes around the shortened principle

parts.note: er is a sound of hesitation

indicators.note: the letter R, for right, is dropped from the principle

parts.note: a rule is a principle

explanation.surface: A mathematician hesitates over a principle he suspects is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's not right' drops the R for right from the principle, and 'about' wraps the hesitation round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was an eighteenth-century Swiss mathematician.

clue.text: Decorated garden lad redesigned

indicators.note: a redesign rearranges things, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young man has had the garden decorated and redesigned.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlanded means adorned with garlands, so decorated.

clue.text: Clever trick group conjured up in cells

parts.note: a game is a scheme or trick, as in 'what's your game?'

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' sends the letters upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: A clever magic trick is performed by a troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conjured up' reverses SET to TES beneath GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Gametes are reproductive cells, sperm or egg, that fuse in fertilisation.

clue.text: Upset as a result of row and left half abandoned

parts.note: a rank is a row, as of soldiers or taxis

indicators.note: half the word is left out, keeping the front half

explanation.surface: Someone is upset after a row and being left by their other half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half abandoned' keeps LE, the first half of LEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle is to cause lasting resentment, to upset or irritate.

clue.text: Freshly dispatched soldiers needing little time to show bitterness

parts.note: re-sent, sent again
men is a common crossword word for soldiers
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Troops are sent out again with barely any time to rest, and grow bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Resentment is the bitter indignation felt at unfair treatment.

clue.text: Refuse encouragement, having taken note

parts.note: a spur is an incentive or encouragement

explanation.surface: Someone takes note of encouragement but turns it down.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn is to reject with contempt, a verb synonym of refuse.

clue.text: Crop: staple source of sustenance, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: a staple is a kind of pin or fastener

indicators.note: the source is where something starts, here the first letter of sustenance

explanation.surface: Thinking about it, a crop such as rice is a staple food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staple' looks like a staple food alongside 'crop'; it is PIN. PIN plus S gives PINS, and 'on reflection' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To crop is to cut short, as does a snip of the scissors.

clue.text: Entrance of some members of top orchestra

indicators.note: only some of the letters, inside the phrase, are taken

explanation.surface: Some players of a leading orchestra make their entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A porch is a covered entrance to a building.

clue.text: Swindle going unchecked puts worker perhaps off

indicators.note: with off, puts off says the worker is taken away from the word
with puts, signals that the worker is removed

parts.note: rampant means spreading unrestrained
an ant is a worker, as in a worker ant

explanation.surface: A runaway fraud scares off a working man.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is British slang for a swindle or racket, especially overcharging.

clue.text: Traveller to ancient city street spanning island

indicators.note: the city and street pieces stretch around the island letter

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A traveller heads to an ancient city whose street crosses an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is someone travelling for pleasure.

clue.text: American football player maybe in old camp

definitions.meaning: a member of a sports league, such as a player in the American NFL
an archaic word for a military camp, especially of a besieging army

explanation.surface: An American footballer turns up in an old army camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaguer covers both a league member and, in old usage, a siege encampment.

clue.text: Woman felt the absence of outspoken type of philosopher

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the phrase is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: Dinah, a woman's name, plus missed, felt the absence of

explanation.surface: A woman misses an outspoken thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, 'Dinah missed' runs together into the philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamist holds that matter or nature is explained by forces, a philosophical position.

clue.text: PM briefly appearing in school to give talk

indicators.note: the shortened prime minister goes inside the school abbreviation
briefly cuts the last letter from the name

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a British prime minister

explanation.surface: A prime minister drops in to a school to address the pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Robert Peel was a nineteenth-century British prime minister; 'briefly' docks his name's last letter before 'appearing in' puts it inside the school.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech is a formal talk given to an audience.
